limitations: Original same-author local research with public fixture issuer keys, plaintext SQLite/bearer/recovery files and unqualified secret BigInt side channels; unsuitable for real assets.

Offline import verifies credential and image binding but does not prove unspent ownership. Issuer submission decides whether a copied file can still be claimed; loss of image metadata can lose bearer authority.
Caller must prepare/normalize images before issuance. Strict PNG shape does not prove pinned-normalizer provenance. Byte-different encodings of the same pixels are different assets.
Image limits are smaller than product image limits; no JPEG or arbitrary PNG support, browser adapter, encrypted vault, wallet endorsement, public proof integration, HTTP listener or hosting.
Public-copy removal excludes the explicit envelope. It does not erase private information deliberately encoded in pixels, compressed data or visible artwork.
Fixed malformed image/JSON cases are not exhaustive fuzzing, independent review, production CPU/admission qualification or all possible decoder tests.

Two copied-image claims are prepared together and submitted sequentially; multiprocess race evidence remains in existing engine tests. No new process-kill locations or filesystem durability qualification.
Demo file readback and mode 0600 do not establish fsync/power-loss, disk failure, permission portability, phone/browser recovery or encrypted backup guarantees.

Wallet bytes remain context only and walletAuthenticated false. State receipts report snapshots, not reservations; malicious issuer, fresh-observer rollback, same/higher-sequence forks and manipulated clocks/trust remain outside guarantees.
C2 local harness complete; C1/C3 partial; independent C4 pending; C5 file prototype only; custody, trust distribution, key lifecycle and C6 hosting remain open.
No live interoperability, audit, production privacy or ordinary MetaMask NFT custody claim. Derived issuer equations and cross-group consistency remain lab choices.
